examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For relation-property questions, apply the definition to every relevant tuple rather than inferring a property from a few pairs. An equivalence relation partitions its set into disjoint nonempty classes. Two elements are related precisely when their classes agree. A function constant on each class induces a well-defined quotient map; injectivity of that map requires different classes to have different images.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
An equivalence relation on a 7-element set has classes of sizes 2,2,3. How many ordered pairs belong to the relation?

**Answer: 17.** Within a class of size k, every element is related to all k members, including itself, giving k² ordered pairs. Across classes there are none. Count=2²+2²+3²=17.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A symmetric relation may contain both (x,y) and (y,x). Antisymmetry allows both only when x=y; it is not the negation of symmetry.

Antisymmetry does not mean “not symmetric”; equality is both symmetric and antisymmetric.
